short: Look-ahead audio-visual master (M02) is new for lip reading but shown on one LRS2 run; confidence curriculum (M03) adds 0.1-1.1 WER points; SOTA claim fails on LRW and LRS3.
position: The paper [@ren2021master] changes the teacher (M02), a trainable audio-visual "master" updated through the loss of a one-step-updated student, and the sample order (M03), a tutor-confidence curriculum. None of 167 prior lip-reading decoders updates a teacher that way (pattern match, Appendix), a mechanism general machine learning already had [@pham2021mpl]; the isolating comparison is one LRS2 value per row, so M02 stays standard. The curriculum is standard: earlier decoders already order by length, contrary to §3.4, and the gain falls to 0.1 WER points on the strongest backend (inference), as the authors concede. The strongest confound: a same-structure video teacher alone gives about half the gain of the best master setting (57.5% to 53.4% WER against 49.6%, Tables 1 and 5; inference). The state-of-the-art claim (M12) holds for public-data sentence rows without an LM, and fails on LRW against born-again distillation [@ma2020towards] and on LRS3 against V2P [@shillingford2018].
